statement: Let $S$ be a smooth projective complex K3 surface and $E$ an elliptic curve, with projections $p,q$. If $\lambda\in H^2(S,\mathbb Z)$ is not in $2H^2(S,\mathbb Z)+\operatorname{im}(c_1:\operatorname{Pic}(S)\to H^2(S,\mathbb Z))$, and $\mu\in H^2(E,\mathbb Z)$, then $\ell=p^*\lambda+q^*\mu\in H^2(S\times E,\mathbb Z)$ is not in $2H^2(S\times E,\mathbb Z)+\operatorname{im}(c_1:\operatorname{Pic}(S\times E)\to H^2(S\times E,\mathbb Z))$.
proof: Let $e_0\in E$ be any point, and let $i:S\to S\times E$ be the closed inclusion $s\mapsto(s,e_0)$. Write $p:S\times E\to S$ and $q:S\times E\to E$ for the projections. Then $p\circ i=\operatorname{id}_S$, and $q\circ i$ is the constant map to $e_0$. Hence for every $\beta\in H^2(E,\mathbb Z)$, $(q\circ i)^*\beta=0$, because the constant map factors through a point and $H^2(\text{point},\mathbb Z)=0$. Consequently, $i^*p^*\lambda=(p\circ i)^*\lambda=\lambda$ and $i^*q^*\mu=(q\circ i)^*\mu=0$ in $H^2(S,\mathbb Z)$. Suppose, toward a contradiction, that $\ell=p^*\lambda+q^*\mu$ lies in $2H^2(S\times E,\mathbb Z)+\operatorname{im}(c_1:\operatorname{Pic}(S\times E)\to H^2(S\times E,\mathbb Z))$. Then there are a class $a\in H^2(S\times E,\mathbb Z)$ and a line bundle $M\in\operatorname{Pic}(S\times E)$ such that $p^*\lambda+q^*\mu=2a+c_1(M)$. Apply $i^*$ and use linearity of pullback together with naturality of the first Chern class: $\lambda=i^*(p^*\lambda+q^*\mu)=i^*(2a+c_1(M))=2i^*a+i^*c_1(M)=2i^*a+c_1(i^*M)$. Because $i^*a\in H^2(S,\mathbb Z)$ and $i^*M\in\operatorname{Pic}(S)$, the right-hand side lies in $2H^2(S,\mathbb Z)+\operatorname{im}(c_1:\operatorname{Pic}(S)\to H^2(S,\mathbb Z))$. This contradicts the hypothesis on $\lambda$. Therefore $\ell$ is not in $2H^2(S\times E,\mathbb Z)+\operatorname{im}(c_1:\operatorname{Pic}(S\times E)\to H^2(S\times E,\mathbb Z))$.

statement: Let X be a smooth connected projective complex variety and L a topological complex line bundle on X. A topological complex vector bundle V of rank two admits a nondegenerate L-valued alternating bilinear form if and only if det(V) is isomorphic to L; the wedge product followed by this isomorphism gives the form, and the resulting class satisfies [V]=[L⊗V^∨] in KU^0(X).
proof:
Proof. Write det(V)=∧²V and V^∨=Hom(V,C). An L-valued alternating bilinear form is a continuous bundle map B:V⊗V→L satisfying B(v⊗w)=-B(w⊗v). By the universal property of the exterior square, B is equivalent to a bundle map β:∧²V→L with β(v∧w)=B(v,w); we identify B and β below.

First suppose B is nondegenerate. For x∈X, let W=V_x and M=L_x. If β_x were zero, then B_x would vanish identically, so the associated map W→Hom(W,M), v↦(w↦B_x(v,w)), would not be injective, contradicting nondegeneracy. Hence β_x is a nonzero map between the one-dimensional vector spaces ∧²W and M, so β_x is an isomorphism. Thus β is a fiberwise isomorphism of vector bundles, hence a vector bundle isomorphism ∧²V≅L. Therefore det(V)≅L.

Conversely, suppose α:det(V)=∧²V→L is a vector bundle isomorphism. Define B(v,w)=α(v∧w). This is bilinear and alternating. For x∈X and 0≠v∈V_x, choose w∈V_x linearly independent of v. Then v∧w is nonzero in ∧²V_x, and α_x is an isomorphism, so B_x(v,w)≠0. Therefore the map ψ_x:V_x→Hom(V_x,L_x), ψ_x(v)(w)=B_x(v,w), is injective. Since both spaces have complex dimension 2, ψ_x is an isomorphism. Thus B is nondegenerate. This proves the equivalence, and it also shows that the form is exactly obtained by wedging and then applying α.

Now use such an isomorphism α. The map ψ:V→V^∨⊗L≅Hom(V,L) given by ψ_x(v)(w)=α_x(v∧w) is a bundle morphism. By the previous paragraph each fiber ψ_x is an isomorphism. Equivalently, choose local frames e_1,e_2 of V and λ of L. Since α is an isomorphism, α(e_1∧e_2)=fλ with f nowhere zero. For v=a e_1+b e_2 and w=c e_1+d e_2 we have ψ(v)(w)=f(ad-bc)λ, so in the bases e_1,e_2 and e_1^*⊗λ,e_2^*⊗λ the matrix of ψ is [[0,-f],[f,0]], with determinant f², nowhere zero. Hence ψ is a vector bundle isomorphism V≅V^∨⊗L.

Tensor product of complex vector bundles is commutative up to canonical isomorphism, so V≅L⊗V^∨. Since isomorphic vector bundles have the same class in the Grothendieck group, [V]=[V^∨⊗L]=[L⊗V^∨] in KU^0(X). This completes the proof.
